1.name: Mainplate (part)
1.note: The base plate that carries the balance and the pallet bearings. It fixes the distance between each pair of pivots.

2.name: Balance cock
2.note: The bridge over the balance. It holds the upper bearing and the hairspring stud.

3.name: Shock block
3.note: Holds the jewels and the lyre spring in each bearing.

4.name: Chaton
4.note: A small setting that carries the hole jewel in the shock block.

5.name: Hole jewel
5.note: The bearing the balance pivot turns in. Ruby is hard enough to keep friction low and constant.

6.name: Cap jewel
6.note: A flat stone that takes the end of the pivot, so it holds the balance's end-float.

7.name: Lyre spring
7.note: A wire spring that lets the jewel move on impact, then returns it to place. A shock cannot snap the pivot.

8.name: Balance staff
8.note: The axle of the balance. It carries the wheel, the hairspring and the roller on two fine pivots.

9.name: Balance
9.note: The oscillating mass. With the hairspring it sets the beat, 4 Hz here, whatever the mainspring does.

10.name: Hairspring
10.note: The restoring spring. It pulls the balance back from each swing and so sets the beat frequency.

11.name: Hairspring collet
11.note: Fixes the inner end of the hairspring to the balance staff.

12.name: Hairspring stud
12.note: Fixes the outer end of the hairspring to the balance cock.

13.name: Double roller
13.note: Two discs on the staff. One carries the impulse jewel and the other is the safety roller that keeps the fork from tripping.

14.name: Impulse jewel
14.note: The balance's finger. Once per beat it enters the fork, unlocks the wheel and takes a push back.

15.name: Pallet fork
15.note: A lever between balance and wheel. It carries the pallet stones and takes the impulse jewel in its notch.

17.name: Entry pallet stone
17.note: Locks a tooth of the wheel, then releases it on cue. The tooth also slides on it, giving impulse to the fork.

18.name: Exit pallet stone
18.note: Same job on the other side. The two stones alternate, so the wheel advances one tooth every two beats.

19.name: Guard pin
19.note: A safety pin at the fork's end. It rides near the safety roller to stop the fork moving if the watch is jarred.

20.name: Escape wheel
20.note: The last gear of the train. It is held by the pallet stones and released a tooth at a time, so it is the stored energy being metered out.

21.name: Escape pinion
21.note: The small gear on the wheel's shaft that the train drives.

22.name: Banking pin
22.note: Two stops that limit how far the fork can swing. They set the lock depth on each stone.
